interface.title: ExoScout
interface.field: Exoplanet astronomy / astronomical machine learning (TESS transit-candidate vetting)
interface.stage_of_work: Candidate vetting and model inspection: you classify one catalog object and probe how the model behaves. No data collection or reduction happens here.
interface.what_it_is_for: Enter (or edit) the seven NASA TESS Object of Interest catalog measurements for one transit candidate and get the frozen v0.5 Random Forest's planet-like vs catalog-false-positive-like call, its uncalibrated score, and the 0.50 threshold it is compared against.

data.note: The form comes pre-filled with one real, planet-like TOI: period 10.07 d, duration 2.40 h, depth 839.90 ppm, TESS mag 9.07, Teff 5552 K, log(g) 4.62, R* 0.79 R☉. Nothing is uploaded or fetched; reloading the page restores these defaults. Classify, the score readout and the input checks are the whole of the app (screens/003.webp, screens/007.webp).

tree.general: Judge whether one candidate's summary measurements look like a real signal or a false alarm, and understand what drives that judgment
tree.specific: Classify a TESS Object of Interest's catalog features with the frozen ExoScout v0.5 Random Forest and probe its decision boundary, missing-data handling and feature sensitivity

features.name: Pre-filled measurement form
features.general: A form of named numeric measurements with units in the labels and a help tooltip per field, pre-filled with a reference record that a reload restores. On submit the inputs are checked and the record is scored.
features.specific: The 'Observation features' form: seven text inputs (period, duration, depth, TESS mag, Teff, log g, R*), each with a ? tooltip, pre-filled with a real TOI. 'Classify observation' sends the record to src/predict.py (confirmed in code, not visible in the browser).
steps: Start from the pre-filled reference record (reload restores it)
Hover a field's ? icon to read its definition
Edit any subset of values
Press Classify observation to score the record
serves_tasks: Look up what an input measures and in what units
Score the reference object and read the call against the decision threshold
Change one measurement step by step and see whether the call flips
Enter a textbook false-alarm profile and check that the model rejects it

features.name: Thresholded score readout with interpretation caveat
features.general: Show a binary call as a coloured banner, the raw model score as a big number and a bar, the fixed cutoff used, and a collapsible note on what the score does and does not mean and which model produced it
features.specific: The 'Model output' panel: a green 'planet-like observation' or yellow 'catalog false-positive-like observation' banner, the 'Uncalibrated planet score' as a percentage with an animated progress bar (which can briefly lag the previous run), 'Frozen classification threshold: 0.50', and the 'How to interpret this result' expander (frozen v0.5 Random Forest; not a calibrated probability; trained on resolved labels, may not generalize to unresolved Planet Candidates)
steps: Submit a record
Read the banner colour and label for the call
Read the percentage score and the bar relative to the 0.50 threshold, after the bar has settled
Optionally expand 'How to interpret this result' for the caveats
serves_tasks: Score the reference object and read the call against the decision threshold
Read the caveats on how to interpret the score
Push a second measurement until the call crosses the threshold

features.name: What-if perturbation loop across a decision threshold (usage pattern over f1 and f2, not a component)
features.general: A way of using a form and a score readout together: repeatedly change one input, re-score, and compare with the last run to find where the call flips and which inputs matter most. The tool keeps no run history, so the comparison is done by hand.
features.specific: Edit one field in the form (f1), for example transit depth 839.9 → 300 → 20 → 30000 or duration 2.4 → 0.8 → 8, press Classify observation, and watch the planet score in the Model output panel (f2) move across 0.50. Each run replaces the previous output; there is no run-history or comparison table.
steps: Classify the baseline record and note the score
Change a single field
Re-classify and compare the score and banner with the noted baseline
Repeat with a larger or opposite change until the banner flips
Reload to reset to the baseline before probing another feature
serves_tasks: Change one measurement step by step and see whether the call flips
Push a second measurement until the call crosses the threshold
Change only the host-star properties, then one at a time, to see which drive the score
Change one transit-shape measurement alone to compare its effect

features.name: Blank-as-missing inputs with imputation and reported missing count
features.general: Let the user leave measurements out by clearing a field. The pipeline fills them in with medians plus a 'was missing' flag and tells you how many it filled, so you can see how incomplete records shift the result.
features.specific: Blank one or more form fields. The output adds a yellow notice 'N missing measurement(s) were handled by the pipeline's median imputation and missingness indicators', and the score changes (one missing radius: 87.1% → 46.4%; six missing: 2.5%). A form with every field blank is refused.
steps: Clear one field and classify
Read the missing-count notice and the new score
Clear further fields and re-classify to see the effect grow
Restore a field (or clear a different one) to compare which missing value matters
serves_tasks: Remove one measurement and compare the call with the complete record
Remove more measurements and see how far the score falls

features.name: Input validation messages
features.general: Refuse to score a record with non-numeric or impossible values, and name the bad field
features.specific: Non-numeric text gives 'pl_trandep must be numeric or missing.'; a negative value gives 'pl_trandep must be greater than zero.'; an all-blank form gives 'Enter at least one measurement before classification.' The red error replaces the Model output panel. Messages use the internal column name (pl_trandep), not the form label.
steps: Type an invalid value (text, a negative number) or blank every field
Press Classify observation
Read the red error naming the offending column, then fix the value
serves_tasks: Check that bad input is rejected and not silently scored

screens_never_reached: No other pages or views exist. The app is one page, and the Main menu holds only Streamlit's own items (theme, Rerun, Auto rerun, Clear cache, Print, Record screen), shown in screens/009.webp.
No feature-importance chart or table in the app. docs/METHODOLOGY.md is not served, so the feature-importance comparison could only be made indirectly, by perturbing inputs.
not_done: Did not confirm the claim that transit geometry dominates over stellar properties. On the default TOI, single-feature changes gave: Teff 3500 alone 89.1% (default 87.1%); stellar radius 3.0 alone 54.3%; duration 8 h alone 69.3%; depth 20–300 ppm 83–87%. Teff/log g/radius changed together gave 14.7%, and one missing stellar radius flipped the call (46.4%). These are local what-if results for one object, not a global importance measure, so they neither confirm nor refute docs/METHODOLOGY.md, but here stellar radius moved the score at least as much as the geometry edits did.

Shrinking transit depth toward zero (20 ppm) did not produce a false-positive call. The suggested 'shallow depth flips it' path did not cross 0.5. The threshold was crossed only with deep (30000 ppm) and long (8 h) transits together, with missing values, or with evolved-star parameters.
The textbook false-alarm profile (t6) was rejected only narrowly: 41.3%, barely below the 41.2% from deep and long transit alone, so adding the short period and evolved star hardly moved the score.
Never typed in a different candidate's full set of seven catalog values; every run started from the default TOI and edited it.

Which two fields were blank in the 41.6% '2 missing' run is not visible on screens/020.webp; the trace (Teff and radius restored to 5552 and 0.79 just afterwards) indicates radius and Teff. The replay cleared radius and log g instead and got 9.7%, a different combination.
No kept screenshot shows the form right after the page reload that began the missing-data runs; the reload is recorded only in the trace.
Could not compare against real catalog dispositions of other TOIs. There is no lookup or list of TOIs in the app, and only the one default object is built in.
Results are not kept between runs. Each Classify replaces the last output, so comparisons were made by reading successive screenshots.

Right after a click the score and bar can show the previous run for a moment (screens/012.webp, screens/015.webp, screens/027.webp showed stale or still-animating values). Every value above was read from a follow-up screenshot after the display had settled.
Did not try the Streamlit-generic menu items (theme switch, Print, Record screen, Clear cache, Deploy). They are not part of the scientific workflow.
